judged_text: The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no try/catch and never checks req.method, so input errors throw instead of returning the 4xx the surrounding code deliberately uses for every other input problem. A GET probe, a request with a missing or ill-typed body, or a wrongly-encrypted keys payload produces an unhandled ZodError or decrypt exception and a Next 500 — breaking the endpoint's own 403/404 contract, leaving the parent-app integrator unable to distinguish auth rejection from server bugs, and dumping stack traces into server logs on every malformed attempt.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does not check `req.method` (so a GET/other method will still execute) and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch. Both `zod.parse` and decrypt/JSON.parse can throw on malformed/missing body or invalid ciphertext, which would surface as an unhandled exception (Next.js 500) rather than the explicit 4xx responses used elsewhere in this handler (403/404).
